【158†llms.txt】 L329: # Autosize L330: L331: The autosize element will automatically adjust the textarea height and make it easier for users to follow as they type. L332: ## Overview L333: L334: A textarea keeps its height no matter how much text it holds, so long answers end up in a small scrolling box. Autosize grows the field as the user types and shrinks it again when text is removed. L335: L336: Autosize example L337: L338: ` L339: ` L340: ## Installation L341: L342: Autosize is part of `tabler.js` and has no dependency, so there is nothing extra to install or load. It only sets the height of the field, so it needs no CSS of its own. L343: ## Usage L344: L345: Add `data-bs-toggle="autosize"` to a textarea. Tabler picks it up on page load, so there is nothing else to call. L346: L347: Message L348: L349: ` L350: ` L351: L352: Set `rows` to choose the starting height. With `rows="1"` the field starts as a single line and grows from there. Set a `max-height` to cap the growth; past it the field scrolls again. L353: Notes, at most four lines L354: L355: ` L356: ` L357: ## JavaScript L358: L359: Tabler ships an `Autosize` component that works like the Bootstrap components: it is created once per element and stored on it. On page load Tabler creates one for every element with `data-bs-toggle="autosize"`. It sets the height from the content on every `input` event and again when the field changes width. This is the code that runs: L360: L361: `initAll(SELECTOR_DATA_TOGGLE, Autosize)` L362: Create the component yourself when you add a textarea later, for example inside a modal or a row added by JavaScript: L363: L364: `const autosize = new tabler.Autosize(document.getElementById('message'));` L365: L366: `tabler.Autosize.getOrCreateInstance(element)` returns the existing component or creates a new one, so it is safe to call more than once for the same field. L367: Autosize measures the field, so a hidden textarea is skipped. Call `update()` once it becomes visible, or after you set its value from code: L368: L369: `tabler.Autosize.getOrCreateInstance(document.getElementById('message')).update();` L370: L371: Call `dispose()` to stop it and put the inline style back the way it was: L372: L373: `tabler.Autosize.getInstance(document.getElementById('message'))?.dispose();` L374: Method | Description L375: --- | --- L376: `update()` | Recalculates the height, for example after the textarea becomes visible or its value changes from code. L377: `dispose()` | Stops listening, restores the inline style and removes the component from the element. L378: `getInstance(element)` | Static. Returns the component for the element, or `null`. L379: `getOrCreateInstance(element)` | Static. Returns the component for the element and creates it when needed. L380: Every change of height fires `resized.bs.autosize` on the textarea, for example to scroll a chat window to the bottom: L381: L382: `document.getElementById('message').addEventListener('resized.bs.autosize', () => { L383: thread.scrollTop = thread.scrollHeight; L384: });` L385: ## Accessibility L386: L387: * Keep the `label` for the field. A growing textarea is still a normal form control and needs its name. L388: * Let the field grow freely when you can. A `max-height` brings back a scrolling box, so keep it generous, for example the height of the visible chat window. L389: * Autosize hides the resize handle, because the field grows on its own. With a `max-height` the field scrolls past the cap, so long text stays reachable. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Form validation states | Tabler UI L354: ## Validation states L355: L356: Validation states mark a field as valid or invalid, so the user sees which fields to correct and, for an invalid one, why. L357: L358: To apply the validation state to the form control, use the `.is-valid` and `.is-invalid` classes. For assistive tech, also set `aria-invalid="true"` on invalid controls. L397: L398: To do this, use the `.is-valid-lite` and `.is-invalid-lite` classes. L399: L400: These variants drop the colored frame and the feedback message, so the state is left to a small icon. Keep `aria-invalid` on the field, and keep the reason in text somewhere the field points to - otherwise the error exists only as a symbol. L415: * Give the feedback element an `id` and point the field at it with `aria-describedby`, so the message is read with the field rather than after the form. L416: * Say what to do, not only what failed. "Please provide a valid city" beats "Invalid". L417: * On submit, move focus to the first field that failed. Otherwise a keyboard user has to hunt for it. L418: * Validate when the user leaves a field, not on every keystroke.
